comparator.name: Computer Science (Informatica)
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–2027 programme-specific OER annex defines a 180-EC Informatica bachelor comprising a 135-EC major and 45-EC profiling space. The major contains 75 EC of compulsory courses, 45 EC chosen from a restricted Informatica list and the compulsory 15-EC Softwareproject. For the generic target, Imperatief programmeren is used rather than the alternative Gameprogrammeren, and the first six officially listed restricted electives are selected: Informatica introductieproject, Computationele intelligentie, Recht en informatica, Webtechnologie, Algoritmiek, and Data-analyse en retrieval. This is a neutral deterministic instantiation of the generic curriculum, not selection of the formal Gametechnologie path or the educational minor. Zero-credit tutorial and guidance activities are excluded from the 180 EC.

alternatives.concept: Builds a UCR computing programme around programming, networks and operating systems, databases, software development, algorithms and mathematical foundations, with data and AI applications. UCR covers substantial computer-science content but has less structured architecture, concurrency, functional programming, web technology and formal capstone training than Utrecht University.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Six four-course semesters in 2026–29, with PPD in Year 1 and at least six 300-level courses. The enriched UCR workbook confirms offerings and all formal prerequisites in earlier semesters; programming and mathematical gates precede advanced computing and AI.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The direct programme interests form one coherent computer-science programme spanning systems, software, algorithms, mathematics, data and AI, and are owned by the closest match. The only separate generator-eligible direction is the educational minor in computer-science teaching. It is not feasible as a distinct 24-course UCR curriculum because UCR lacks the subject didactics, supervised school placement and teaching-qualification structure that define that route. Curricular topics and career outcomes support the closest match but cannot generate additional alternatives.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Introduction to Programming directly addresses imperative programming in Python, with different scope and credits.
Logic & Discrete Mathematics directly addresses logic for computer science, with different scope and credits.
Algorithms & Data Structures directly addresses the data-structures requirement, with different scope and credits.
Advanced Algorithms directly addresses the selected Algoritmiek elective, with different scope and credits.
Probability & Statistics supplies quantitative research methods, but does not reproduce the comparator’s dedicated computer-science research-methods course.
UCR has no selected course that reproduces the compulsory functional-programming component.
UCR has no selected course that reproduces the compulsory concurrency component.
Networks & Operating Systems directly addresses the networking portion, but does not reproduce the comparator’s computer-architecture depth.
Database Management Systems directly addresses the databases component, with different scope and credits.
Software Development addresses software design, testing and maintenance, though the comparator has a dedicated software-engineering requirement.
Consumer Product Design supplies team-based iterative project practice, but is not an informatics-specific introductory project.
AI Ethics and general Ethics provide normative analysis, but UCR has no selected course in information-technology law.
UCR has no selected dedicated web-technology course.
UCR’s optional independent-research opportunity is shown separately against the compulsory 15-EC Softwareproject; it is not part of the fixed 180-EC UCR programme.
The genuine 45-EC profiling space is preserved without inventing a specific Utrecht minor, exchange or elective package.
Introduction to Data Science addresses the data-analysis portion of Data-analyse en retrieval, with broader introductory scope.
Image Processing & Computer Vision addresses visual computing, but not the full computer-graphics scope of the comparator component.
Decision-making in AI directly supports computational intelligence, with different scope and credits.

notes.text: Utrecht University requires computer architecture, functional programming, concurrency, web technology, IT law, a 15-EC Softwareproject and a structured Informatica major. UCR can build a substantial programme in programming, databases, networks and operating systems, software, algorithms, mathematics, data science and AI, but it does not reproduce that full specialist sequence or compulsory capstone.
